gaps.info: Femoral pulse quality and presence/delay (radiofemoral delay)
gaps.discriminates: Coarctation vs. renal artery stenosis or essential hypertension — coarctation requires physical evidence of distal perfusion compromise; renal causes lack pulse delay.

gaps.info: Presence, location, and character of cardiac murmur (e.g., systolic ejection murmur over back/left scapula)
gaps.discriminates: Coarctation vs. aortic stenosis — coarctation murmur is typically posterior/infrascapular; aortic stenosis murmur is right upper sternal border with radiation to carotids.

gaps.info: Four-limb blood pressure measurements (including both arms and at least one leg) with documented gradient magnitude (e.g., ≥20 mmHg arm-leg difference)
gaps.discriminates: Coarctation vs. Takayasu arteritis or other large-vessel vasculitides — coarctation shows fixed, focal gradient; Takayasu may show asymmetric involvement of multiple branches without classic arm-leg gradient.
